messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from today's design review — we still need to pick an approach for edge backpressure + retry semantics.

maria: TL;DR: choose one of these: 1) explicit handshake token for streaming resumption, 2) header-based graceful backpressure with buffering on edge, or 3) always passthrough and rely on client-level retries.

sam: I'd vote for explicit handshake. Keeps data plane stateless for retries, easier to reason about KV cache validity.

jin: handshake is neat but adds round-trip and state we must manage. Where would we persist the handshake meta? Redis? etcd? disk?

lina: We could keep a short-lived in-memory mapping per gateway pod + leader sync for cross-pod failover. That reduces latency but complicates failover.

maria: Tradeoffs: in-memory -> fast but N+1 failover; persistent store -> consistent resume but higher tail latency and cost.

sam: Also need to define idempotency surface. If we allow resume mid-stream, how do we guarantee duplicate tokens aren't replayed across models? I suggest an "X-Redwood-Resume-ID" + model-pin to validate.

alex: Agreed. Proposal: handshake produces a resume token bound to (customer_id, model_version, prompt_hash, seq_window). Token TTL short: 30s-2m.

jin: If TTL is short, clients need faster retry backoff. We should also support an "opaque checkpoint" header for client-sent checkpoints: `X-Resume-Checkpoint: base64(<kv_state>)`.

lina: Yikes, checkpoint payload size matters. We should cap to 2KB and reject larger. Do we compress? maybe zstd.

sam: Another option: don't do checkpoints in client; instead do prefix caching on the runtime and expose cache-key to client. Simpler for SDKs.

deploy-bot: build #3482: edge-handshake-prototype pushed to canary

maria: Buffering tradeoff: whole-response buffer = high mem. Streaming passthrough keeps mem low but can't retry partial failures. We can do micro-buffers per-connection (32KB sliding window) so retries can resume within small window.

alex: Good point. Micro-buffer + resume token that includes byte offset seems reasonable. That means resume only within last N tokens, otherwise fallback to restart.

jin: Observability: we need span correlation across handshake, streaming segments, and backend calls. Add `x-rw-trace-id` and include resume token in logs (hashed).

lina: Also rate-limiting interplay: token reuse should decrement quota only once. So resume should be charged to the original request id, not the retry id.

sam: Edge case: client aborts and reconnects with same token immediately — race with server-side flush. We need lease semantics: token in-use flag held for 100ms after disconnect.

maria: Action items: 1) draft small RFC with: handshake proto (HTTP preflight POST /v1/resume), token schema, TTL, micro-buffer sizing, charge semantics. 2) prototype in edge canary. 3) SDK patch to support resume header. Volunteers?

alex: I'll draft RFC. @sam @jin can you prototype micro-buffer in runtime? @lina can you spec observability fields? I'll add SDK changes to backlog.

sam: on it

jin: ok

lina: will write observability spec

alex: thanks all :thumbsup:
